newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 13 people killed in Mogadishu attack, witnesses.
newsitem.headline: 13 people killed in Mogadishu attack, witnesses.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen killed 13 people and wounded 16 on Tuesday in an attack on a south Mogadishu restaurant in an area loyal to Somali faction leader Hussein Aideed.
Witnesses said the gunmen sped up to the Muna restaurant near the largest market in south Mogadishu and fired a rocket -propelled grenade into it and raked it with machinegunfire.
A total of 13 people including one woman were killed and 16 wounded and taken to al-Imra hospital in south Mogadishu.
The gunmen escaped on a four-wheel-drive pickup. Most of the dead were members of the same sub-clan as Aideed, who took over from his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August.

South Mogadishu has been hit since September by a string of assassinations, attacks and counter-attacks which Somali experts say are part of a vendetta between groups over Mohamed Farah Aideed's death.

Since last month supporters of Aideed have killed more than 10 people who backed Hassan Ali Osman Atto, a rival south Mogadishu faction leader whose forces are widely blamed for killing Mohamed Farah Aideed.
Aideed, like his father, was elected president of Somalia by supporters and heads a government. But it has not received much international recognition and is rejected by most other leaders.
In another incident, a Somali employee of the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation was killed when unidentified gunmen attacked his car in south Mogadishu on Monday night.

Tuesday's killings were the latest breach of an agreement in principle on October 15 between factions including Aideed's to make peace brokered by Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi in talks in Nairobi.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow by rebels of late dictator president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
